items.title: trump puts a date on it: strike iran sunday, or sign a deal
items.summary:
trump said the us could attack iran as soon as sunday or reach what he called a big, beautiful deal, after tehran blamed washington for the interim deal collapsing.
pezeshkian called the americans cowards who messed everything up but said both sides should come back and conclude it; the irgc warns any strike gets a response several times greater.
items.change: trump moved from 'may do another little epic fury' to naming sunday as the window, and iran's chief of staff said us forces will not be allowed in the gulf 'at any time'.

items.title: tehran widens its target list to gulf energy and airports
items.summary:
iran has warned publicly and through diplomatic channels that a new campaign would bring strikes on gas pipelines, airports and civilian infrastructure around the gulf, per a wall street journal report cited by the jerusalem post.
parliament's foreign affairs chair asked for permission to use 'deterrent weapons, including nuclear', and to suspend npt cooperation if the us attacks.
items.change: new this build: the threat list now names gulf pipelines, airports and civilian sites, and a nuclear option was raised by name in parliament.

meta.reported_by: Wall Street Journal via Jerusalem Post

items.title: houthis hit aramco sites and riyadh airport, and missiles fly at mecca and medina
items.summary:
saudi civil defence said it intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at the mecca and medina regions, with debris falling in jeddah, taif and rabigh.
the houthis said they hit aramco's yanbu facility, the rabigh refinery and king khalid airport in riyadh, and called the holy-city claim a huge lie, saying their targets were airports, oil sites and an airbase.
items.change: the targets jumped from taif and yanbu to riyadh's main airport plus two aramco sites, and for the first time in this round the missiles were aimed at the two holy cities.

items.title: aden's airport takes a fourth missile hit this month
items.summary:
two ballistic missiles hit aden international airport, the fourth attack on it this month, and the houthis also struck the coastguard headquarters, yemen's government said.
a houthi missile that malfunctioned killed three people in a family home in sanaa, and the houthis say saudi strikes hit sanaa and hodeidah, a claim riyadh has not confirmed.
items.change: new this build: aden airport has now been hit four times this month and the coastguard headquarters was struck as well.

items.title: israel empties 2,000 more palestinians from hebron
items.summary:
the idf and shin bet forced about 2,000 palestinians out of their homes in hebron, demolished structures and searched 200 locations after two soldiers were killed on friday.
ten suspects were arrested in the sweep, and the bbc reports palestinian families displaced as the demolition work carries on.
items.change: the operation widened from razing one neighbourhood to a district-wide evacuation of about 2,000 people, with 200 locations searched and 10 arrested.

items.title: 100,000 rally in tel aviv two days before the vote
items.summary:
more than 100,000 people filled tel aviv's hostage square on saturday demanding a state commission of inquiry into the october 7 failures, with opposition leaders beside the families.
israelis vote on tuesday, with netanyahu's coalition under pressure and arab parties likely holding the balance of power.
items.change: the protest grew from thousands midweek to more than 100,000 on saturday night, the biggest rally of the campaign.

items.title: jordan's church toll is still disputed at seven or nine, and nobody is in custody
items.summary:
gunmen opened fire on a greek orthodox funeral in karak on friday and the count still differs: the guardian reports nine dead and 40 hurt, while the bbc and ap say seven.
the us embassy says security has been ramped up in jordan, and two days on no arrests have been announced.
items.change: the toll is now reported as seven by the bbc and ap and nine by the guardian, and the us embassy confirmed it raised security in jordan.

items.title: us embassies harden as washington warns iran is hunting its people
items.summary:
the us intelligence chief said iran is trying harder to target american personnel in the region, and american embassies tightened security ahead of the november 3 midterms.
the state department also updated its israel travel advisory on friday as the threat picture widened.
items.change: the warning moved from a general threat picture to embassies visibly tightening security and a fresh travel advisory for israel.

items.title: wall street ends the week lower as the ai trade wobbles
items.summary:
the s&p fell 0.52% to 7,623.68 on friday and 0.47% on the week; the nasdaq lost 0.21% to 25,955.34 and 0.71% on the week.
the dow slipped 1.24% on friday but still gained 0.41% for the week; the vix closed at 19.45.

items.title: everything is shut, and monday's open is a coin flip on iran
items.summary:
cash markets and futures are closed for the weekend, so friday's levels are the last prices: s&p 7,623.68, nasdaq 25,955.34, dow 52,215.16, vix 19.45.
equity and oil futures reopen at 6pm et on sunday, 1am monday in riyadh, straight into a weekend where trump floated a strike on iran as soon as sunday.

items.title: oil closed at a six-month high on iran war fears, and aramco cleared its headquarters
items.summary:
brent settled at $116.72, up 3.1%, and wti at $103.27, up 3.8%, with brent 6.2% higher on the week and up for a third straight week.
aramco told staff to leave its dhahran headquarters and work remotely, and washington ordered non-essential diplomats out of saudi arabia.

items.title: the fed decides wednesday and four megacaps report into it
items.summary:
the fomc decides on wednesday, with q3 gdp and september pce both due thursday at 8:30am et.
alphabet and microsoft report wednesday after the close, amazon thursday after the close, and exxon, abbvie and chevron close the week on friday.

items.title: nvidia's role as the ai financier hits its first stress test
items.summary:
nvidia carries $36bn of off-balance-sheet backstops for neoclouds plus a guarantee of up to $105bn for openai's ohio site, and the credit market is now pricing the risk.
coreweave, nebius and iren are down at least 30% this month, coreweave's cds spread is past 11%, and firmus pulled its ipo.

items.title: france's borrowing costs sit at a 2002 high as the protests spread across europe
items.summary:
violence spread across several european cities overnight, with about 100 arrested in barcelona and clashes in italy, as the french budget fight resumes on october 27.
french yields are at their highest since 2002 and moody's kept the country at aa3 with a negative outlook on friday.

items.title: robert half jumped 22% on a q3 beat while lkq lost a fifth of its value
items.summary:
robert half closed up 21.7% at $45.87, the s&p's biggest gainer, after third-quarter earnings beat estimates and calmed margin fears.
lkq fell 22.5% to $17.42 on weak preliminary results and an ousted chief executive; corcept dropped 20.1%, bloom energy 11.2% and credo 9.5%.

items.title: gold lost 4.1% in a week when a war premium was building in oil
items.summary:
gold closed at $4,007.90, down 1.3% on friday and 4.1% on the week, even as brent added 6.2% on iran strike risk.
the divergence is the tell for monday: either the war bid pulls gold back or positioning keeps unwinding into the fed.

items.title: brighton at anfield at 2pm, with a storm outside and the top four on the line
items.summary:
liverpool host brighton at anfield on sunday at 2pm gmt, 5pm in riyadh, needing a win to strengthen their push for the top four.
it is the fifth game of nine in 28 days across three competitions, and iraola says he will keep rotating tired legs.

items.title: storm boelo puts a yellow wind warning over anfield
items.summary:
the met office has a yellow wind warning over merseyside until 9pm on sunday, with gusts above 50mph expected around kick-off.
merseyrail is running some of its first trains empty to check the lines, and fans are being warned about delays and flying debris.

items.title: szoboszlai is out, munoz is a doubt, and gravenberch is available again
items.summary:
szoboszlai is out with the hamstring problem he aggravated at brentford, munoz is a doubt with the knock from the same game, and barcola trained normally after sitting out thursday.
gravenberch is back after serving a one-match league ban, while bradley, ekitike and leoni stay long-term absentees and endo and chiesa return to the squad.

items.title: brighton arrive without mitoma, ferguson and tzimas
items.summary:
brighton are missing kaoru mitoma, zadok yohanna, stefan tzimas and evan ferguson, while yankuba minteh and mats wieffer could return after months out.
hurzeler said the pair will train with the group but may be saved for the manchester city games, and struijk and azeez are doubts.

items.title: iraola says wirtz is judged on body language, not output
items.summary:
iraola defended florian wirtz after another quiet game, saying cold body language doesn't do the player any favours with a crowd waiting for a goal.
wirtz is expected to keep his place against brighton as liverpool manage a nine-game run in 28 days.

items.title: ngumoha is set to start again after the villarreal night
items.summary:
rio ngumoha is expected to start against brighton after his breakthrough against villarreal, with barcola fit and iraola rotating a tired squad.
the echo says iraola now has a player he cannot drop, with the teenager keeping his place ahead of more established options.

items.title: liverpool tell valencia they will trigger otorbi's £25m clause
items.summary:
liverpool have contacted valencia to say they intend to activate the £25m exit clause of right winger david otorbi, according to a teamtalk report carried on the club's media watch page.
valencia have taken steps to block the exit; reliability: one outlet, unconfirmed by either club.

items.title: chelsea on wednesday without palmer, banned after two yellows
items.summary:
chelsea visit in the carabao cup on wednesday and will be without cole palmer, sent off for two yellow cards in their league defeat at tottenham.
the ban carries into the cup, so he returns for chelsea's league game with manchester united; arsenal follow liverpool after that.
